reviews.title: Who Knew?
reviews.text:
As a lover of language (and teacher) I think there is no better English dictionary app than Merriam-Webster Dictionary+. 
I appreciate the clear listing of definitions, audio pronunciations (especially valuable for English language learners) and, my personal favorite, Word of the Day, which not only provides new insights into language that I may or may not be familiar with, but does so with clever, well-wrought commentary. 
Bravo!

reviews.title: Hands down best dictionary app
reviews.text: Not only is it the best dictionary app on my phone, it’s probably the best designed app I’ve ever used. It’s been on my phone for more than a decade so I don’t recall if I coughed up money for the ad-free version or not but if I did, it was a one-time affair and a good use of money. There’s no in-app purchases offered. It’s useful, and unexpectedly, entertaining. It doesn’t get in the way of my workflow with distracting notifications. That may be my personal settings but turning off or limiting notifications on other apps often doesn’t work or reduces the functionality of the app. I could go on about my satisfaction with the M-W app, but won’t. I’ll just say, if you are debating a dictionary app, others are excellent too but eventually get sunsetted. This one will withstand the test of time, is the best source for definitions anyway, and its thesaurus is excellent and easy to use too—no more writer’s block!

reviews.title: An Honest Offline Dictionary
reviews.text:
I am returning to this review to give the app top marks. It is a very good reference and works fine with no internet connection. It's the best dictionary app I have found. Thank you Merriam-Webster.

A few minutes ago I down-rated this dictionary, because it lacked a word I sought. Then I went back to the app store, looking again for a more comprehensive offline dictionary. I chose one that actually had "Offline" in its title. What lie. It was actually a vehicle for subscription services, and would not even let me look up a word without accepting a free trial. Deleted it. Thanks again, M-W for an honest app.

reviews.title: Weak definitions
reviews.text: I really messed up purchasing this. Merriam-Webster is pretty surface level compared to the OED. But beyond the shallow definitions, the app doesn’t seem formatted for the larger iPhones and the UI is surprisingly sparse (not in a good way). Also, there’s no search history or an ability to download anything. These are basic features I’ve seen in nearly every other dictionary app. I feel like a sucker having paid $10 for this. Sigh.

reviews.title: I use this every day!
reviews.text:
When I was a child, my father — a university law professor and a remarkably knowledgeable man — kept a huge dictionary on the coffee table as the centerpiece of our living room. Whenever we asked the meaning of a word, he would simply say, “Go look it up in the dictionary!”

That habit gave my siblings and me a strong vocabulary — and, I believe, helped us build good careers through our own merit, not through recommendations.

As a non-native English speaker, I now use this app every day, and it has become my modern dictionary.

The only danger? As someone with ADHD, I sometimes get happily lost in the brilliantly designed word games. Thankfully, I’m retired!

Kudos to M-W!
